newsitem.title: UK: Nomura consortium agrees British army housing buy.
newsitem.headline: Nomura consortium agrees British army housing buy.

text.p: Britain's Ministry of Defence said on Tuesday it would sell 57,400 married quarters for 1.662 billion stg to a group called Annington in a transaction underwritten by Nomura International.
Nomura will also hold the majority of the risk capital of Annington, which will draw on the property service expertise of construction and facilities management group AMEC Plc.
The bulk of funding for the acquisition will be provided by Abbey National Treasury Services, Hambros Bank, the Midland Bank and the Royal Bank of Scotland, the ministry said in a statement.
"We have secured a very good price for the tax payer in a highly competitive auction," said James Arbuthnot, Minister of State for Defence Procurement.
"Service families will start to see the benefits as a massive programme of housing improvement, made possible by the sale, comes on stream," he added.
Completion of the deal is expected in six weeks' time. The purchase price will be payable on completion, minus 700 million stg which will be deferred until 1 April 1997.
Of the proceeds, 100 million stg will be earmarked for a programme to upgrade married quarters throughout Britain.
The deal was widely expected after the The Times newspaper on September 3 reported that a Nomura-led group had been selected to buy the married quarters.
The defence ministry said Annington agreed to offer army personnel attractively-priced mortgages and discounted prices to buy houses from the group.
Furthermore, Annington will set up a trust to benefit army families by sponsoring community activities and projects.
It is expected that most of the minority share of risk capital not provided by Nomura will be taken by New York-based investment fund Blackrock Capital Finance LP, the ministry said.

"The new arrangements give us the flexibility we need to tackle the problem of empty Ministry of Defence homes, and concentrate on the quarters we need, not the ones we don't," said Arbuthnot. The defence ministry said that further housing sales are planned for the years ahead as fewer quarters are needed.
